Hi Alex & Sophie - quick technical note addressing your Qs. I'm happy to go deeper on the call. High-level patterns we recommend:

1) Auth + SDK setup
- SDKs support custom auth hooks; for your case we recommend short-lived JWTs (1-5m) minted by your KMS and exchanged for a Redwood session token. Our SDK provides an auth callback to refresh tokens transparently. See gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/sdk-auth-example
- For private routing you can terminate TLS at your gateway and forward the Redwood session token in an Authorization header.

2) Constrained decoding + schema enforcement
- Use a two-layer approach: (a) constrained decoding at generation time (token-level constraints / allowed-token vocab for field names) to reduce hallucinations, and (b) strict post-parse validation against your JSON Schema.
- We provide a constrained-decoding parameter (schema_profile) in the SDK to bias generation to your schema. Example pseudo-config: schema_profile: { mode: "constrained", required_fields: ["product_id","price_cents"], field_tokens: {...} }
- Always run server-side validation as the final gate: if validation fails, return a structured error with diagnostics (path, rule, offending token indices).

3) Retry and idempotency patterns
- Recommended flow: on validation failure, do deterministic re-generation with stronger constraints (e.g., increase constraint weight, reduce sampling temperature, or switch to beam search). Track a request_id and max_attempts (2-3).
- If the generation is non-deterministic and you need strict idempotency, persist the last-valid output or use an approval hook before ingest.

4) Embeddings + reranker stage
- Typical pattern: generate N candidates (top-k) using the structured output flow, compute embeddings for each candidate with Redwood's embeddings endpoint, then run a reranker model or similarity scoring to pick the best candidate for ingestion. This avoids forcing a single output from the generator and improves downstream precision.

Attachments: I've attached a short SDK setup PDF and a JSON with schema examples (redwood-sdk-setup.pdf, structured-output-guidelines.json).
